ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows two adjacent lower unit squares sharing a vertical edge, and one upper unit square centered above that shared edge. A straight diagonal runs from the upper-left corner of the top square down to the lower-right corner of the lower-right square. The shaded region is the part of the top square on the right side of this diagonal together with a triangular part in the lower-right square. Reasoning: Place the two lower squares on 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, 0 ≤ y ≤ 1, with their common edge at x = 1. Since the top square is centered above that common edge and has side length 1, it occupies 0.5 ≤ x ≤ 1.5, 1 ≤ y ≤ 2. The diagonal goes from (0.5, 2) to (2, 0). Its vertical drop is 2 and horizontal run is 1.5. After dropping 1 unit from y = 2 to y = 1, it moves horizontally 0.75, so it meets y = 1 at x = 1.25. In the top square, the unshaded triangular part has base 0.75 and height 1, so its area is (1/2)(0.75)(1) = 3/8. Thus the shaded part of the top square has area 1 - 3/8 = 5/8. In the lower-right square, the shaded triangle has base 0.75 and height 1, so its area is 3/8. Adding the shaded areas gives 5/8 + 3/8 = 1 cm^2.

The shaded parts lie in the upper square and the lower-right square, separated by a straight diagonal running from the upper-left corner of the top square to the lower-right corner of the lower-right square. Use coordinates: put the lower squares on 0≤x≤2, 0≤y≤1, so their common edge is x=1, and the top square is 0.5≤x≤1.5, 1≤y≤2. The diagonal goes from (0.5,2) to (2,0). Its total vertical drop is 2 and horizontal run is 1.5, so after dropping 1 unit it has moved 0.75 horizontally, meeting y=1 at x=1.25. In the top square, the unshaded triangular part has base 0.75 and height 1, area 3/8, so the shaded top part has area 1−3/8=5/8. In the lower-right square, the shaded triangle has base 0.75 and height 1, area 3/8. Add 5/8+3/8=1 cm².

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the gray region consists of a portion of the top square and a portion of the lower-right square on the same side of one straight slanted line. The top square is horizontally centered over the shared edge of the two lower squares. Instead of computing separate triangle areas, compare paired horizontal slices. Since the top square is centered, the diagonal from the upper-left corner of the top square to the lower-right corner of the lower-right square has horizontal run 1.5 cm and vertical drop 2 cm, so its horizontal shift per 1 cm vertical change is 0.75 cm. For a slice t cm below the top of the upper square, the gray width in the upper square is 1−0.75t. For the corresponding slice t cm above the bottom of the lower-right square, the gray width in the lower-right square is 0.75t. The two widths add to 1 for every 0≤t≤1. Therefore the combined shaded area over height 1 is exactly the area of a 1-by-1 square, namely 1 cm².
